taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes that one study nests Regina septemvittata within Nerodia and another relates it to Tropidoclonion; Crother (2017) retained Regina pending further study.
fieldMarks: Slender semiaquatic snake, 34-92 cm; brownish or olive above with a yellow stripe along each side extending onto the lip scales.
Belly bright yellow with four brownish lengthwise stripes converging toward the tail.
Keeled scales (19 rows at midbody), round pupils, divided anal plate; no light stripe down the back, unlike garter snakes.
Young show dark horizontal bands on the back.
behavior: Eats almost exclusively crayfish, preferring freshly molted ones; occasionally small fish and amphibian larvae.
Diurnal and solitary outside breeding; basks on rocks, logs and branches overhanging the water.
Active May-September in the north, and year-round in warm climates; hibernates in crayfish or mammal burrows in the north.
Live-bearing; 5-31 young born July to early September.
habitat: Occurs only where crayfish are abundant, generally in moderate to fast-flowing streams with rocky or sandy bottoms, cover and sun exposure.
Sometimes uses ditches, canals, marsh or pond edges, but is usually scarce there.
range: Eastern United States from the southern Great Lakes to the Florida panhandle and east to the Carolinas, north to Pennsylvania and New York; in Canada only southern Ontario (Georgian Bay, Bois Blanc Island), ranked N2 and listed Endangered under SARA.

lookalikes.name: Garter snakes
lookalikes.howToTell: Garter snakes have a light dorsal stripe and an undivided anal plate; queen snakes lack a dorsal stripe and have a divided anal plate (Animal Diversity Web).
